title: `mv <TAB><BS><TAB>`: a second completion on a zsh/files builtin name drew no listing

observed.measured: 2026-09-14, a pinned, re-codesigned copy of target/debug/zshrs built at 7f0c69113a (zshrs 0.12.64, 113616528 bytes, sha256 5542a9533839f466) vs zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0), --jobs 1, also at --settle 1200
observed.notes: Before dd61c02640 the second TAB (command position, word `mv`) drew nothing where zsh lists `mv mview mvim mvimdiff mvimex mvn mvnDebug mvnyjp`; fingerprint 3e189505ba. The same defect covered `chmod ` (4a0f2f20b6), `mkdir `/`rmdir ` (ebc8295378) and `ln ` (6ec692b03c) — every one a zsh/files module builtin name; `cp `, which zsh/files does not define, always passed. The ported `_set_command`/`_shadow` answered `$+builtins[X]` from `createbuiltintable()`, which holds every statically linked module's builtins, where C's getpmbuiltin (c:Src/Modules/parameter.c:784-799) reports only loaded, enabled ones. dd61c02640 routed both through `shared::plus_builtins`.

why_this_fixture_exists: The divergence was recorded OPEN in scripts/comptab_divergent_cases.txt as a list-state residue (lastambig/menucmp/validlist/...) and was instead fixed as a side effect of a `$builtins` accessor change, without any cell covering it. A later change that re-widens `$+builtins` to the static table (or loads zsh/files by default) brings it back silently; this cell is the only guard.

controls.note: `cp ` is not a zsh/files builtin; it passed before and after the fix, so the split is the command name, not the key sequence.

variants.note: same defect, described-listing shape (zsh: `a -- all` .. `+ - \=`; zshrs before the fix: nothing).
